title: Local cancellation of a residue-exact finite-free degree
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p$ a prime ideal, $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$ (the field of fractions $\bar x/\bar s$ with $\bar s\ne0$, where $\bar x/\bar s=\bar y/\bar t$ if $\bar x\bar t=\bar y\bar s$), and $i\in\mathbf Z$. Let $P^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], each term having a finite basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Suppose $H^i(P^\bullet\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))=0$. There exist $f\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and a complex $Q^\bullet$ of finite free $R_f$-modules, where $R_f=R[1/f]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], with a chain homotopy equivalence $P^\bullet\otimes_R R_f\simeq Q^\bullet$ (chain maps whose composites differ from the identities by $dh+hd$, with $h$ of degree $-1$), such that $Q^i=0$. For $j\notin\{i-1,i,i+1\}$ its terms and differentials between such terms agree with those of $P^\bullet\otimes_R R_f$; its terms in degrees $i-1$ and $i+1$ are finite free direct summands of the corresponding original terms. In particular every degree in which $P$ is zero remains zero in $Q$.

proof.text: Choose finite bases in degrees $i-1,i,i+1$. Extension of a basis is a basis: $(a_j)\mapsto\sum e_j\otimes a_j$ and $e_j\otimes a\mapsto a$ in coordinate $j$ are inverse by bilinearity. Prove the claim by induction on the number $m$ of middle basis vectors, uniformly for all rings, primes and complexes. For $m=0$, take $f=1$, $Q=P\otimes_R R_1$, identity maps and zero homotopy; $Q^i=0$ because its basis is empty.

source.place: Tag 068U, lemma-cut-complex-in-two, direct matrix proof expanded into unit-entry induction

proof.text: For $m>0$, write the incoming and outgoing matrices as $A,B$. If both residue matrices were zero, $H^i$ of the residue complex would be $\kappa(\mathfrak p)^m\ne0$ (its first coordinate vector is nonzero). Choose a nonzero residue entry of either matrix, represented by $a\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$, and invert $a$. The map $R_a\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ sends $x/a^t$ to $\bar x/\bar a^t$; its kernel is $\mathfrak p_a=\{x/a^t:x\in\mathfrak p\}$, which is prime because its image lies in a field and is a domain. Its quotient embeds in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and every element $\bar x/\bar s$ of that field is the quotient of the images of $x/1$ and $s/1$, with the latter nonzero. This identifies its fraction field with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The inverse scalar-extension maps are $(z\otimes u)\otimes v\mapsto z\otimes uv$ and $z\otimes v\mapsto(z\otimes1)\otimes v$, with balancing and inverse identities checked on pure tensors. They commute with differentials, so the residue complex and its vanishing hypothesis are unchanged.

source.place: Tag 068U, lemma-cut-complex-in-two, direct matrix proof expanded into unit-entry induction

proof.text: For the selected differential $D:S^u\to S^v$ over $S=R_a$, permute bases so its unit entry is at $(1,1)$, and rescale the first source vector to $e=a^{-1}e_1$. Put $w=D(e)$; its first coordinate is $1$. The vectors $(w,t_2,\ldots,t_v)$ are a target basis: subtract the first coordinate times $w$ to obtain the remaining coefficients. For each other source vector subtract its first image coordinate times $e$. These invertible triangular changes give $D=\operatorname{diag}(1,D_0)$. No constancy of residue ranks over an open is asserted.

proof.text: The selected degree is $k=i-1$ or $k=i$. From $d^kd^{k-1}=0$ the preceding differential has zero component in the first source coordinate; from $d^{k+1}d^k=0$ the succeeding differential kills the first target vector. Hence the complex is $C\oplus T$, where $T$ is $S\xrightarrow{1}S$ in degrees $k,k+1$, zero elsewhere. Projection $p_1$ and inclusion $q_1$ are chain maps with $p_1q_1=1$. Define $h_1^{k+1}$ to send the first target coordinate to the first source coordinate and all other components to zero. Substitution in each degree gives $1-q_1p_1=dh_1+h_1d$. The middle basis size of $C$ is $m-1$; only these two terms have shrunk to explicit complementary spans.

source.place: Tag 068U, lemma-cut-complex-in-two, direct matrix proof expanded into unit-entry induction

proof.text: Tensor these equations with the residue field; functoriality and linearity preserve them. For any cycle $z$, $(dh_1+h_1d)z=d(h_1z)$ is a boundary, so $p_1,q_1$ induce inverse cohomology maps. Thus $H^i(C\otimes\kappa(\mathfrak p))=0$. Apply induction over $S=R_a$ and the prime kernel above to obtain a further element $g$ outside that prime and a model with middle term zero. Write $g=b/a^t$, with $b\notin\mathfrak p$. Then $(R_a)_g\cong R_{ab}$: inverting $a,b$ inverts $g$, and inverting $a,g$ inverts $b=ga^t$. Explicitly the maps send $(x/a^r)/g^s$ to $xb^{-s}a^{ts-r}$ in $R_{ab}$ and $x/(ab)^n$ to $xa^{-n}(ga^t)^{-n}$ in $(R_a)_g$; substituting $g=b/a^t$ verifies both composites on fractions. For each term, the scalar-extension maps $(z\otimes u)\otimes v\mapsto z\otimes uv$ and $z\otimes v\mapsto(z\otimes1)\otimes v$ are balanced inverses commuting with every differential and every homotopy. These identify the twice-extended original complex with $P\otimes_R R_{ab}$. Thus $ab\notin\mathfrak p$ supplies one principal localization.

source.place: Tag 068U, lemma-cut-complex-in-two, direct matrix proof expanded into unit-entry induction

proof.text: After this localization, let $p_2:C\to Q$, $q_2:Q\to C$ be the induction maps, with $1-q_2p_2=dh_2+h_2d$ and $1-p_2q_2=dt_2+t_2d$. Set $p=p_2p_1$, $q=q_1q_2$. Expanding gives $1-qp=d(h_1+q_1h_2p_1)+(h_1+q_1h_2p_1)d$; since $p_1q_1=1$, also $1-pq=dt_2+t_2d$. Hence these are the required homotopy equivalence maps. Outside $i-1,i,i+1$ all basis changes and cancellations are identities, so terms and differentials between them are unchanged. Successive finite free complementary spans are direct summands of the original terms: $F=U\oplus V$ and $U=U'\oplus W$ give $F=U'\oplus(W\oplus V)$. Zero terms remain zero. Induction terminates, proving every clause.
